My research develops learning and signal-processing methods for data with **relational and multi-domain structure**. I am particularly interested in methods that combine mathematical structure, scalable learning, and interpretable representations.

## Research directions

### Graph machine learning and graph neural networks

I study learning architectures for graph-structured data, with emphasis on principled graph filters, continuous formulations, scalability, stability, and the behavior of deep graph models.

### Graph signal processing and graph learning

A central theme of my work is learning graph structure from observed signals and exploiting graph spectral structure for inference, forecasting, source separation, and representation learning.

### Higher-order and multi-domain structures

My recent research extends graph learning beyond pairwise interactions to product graphs, simplicial complexes, hypergraphs, and related higher-order structures. This includes continuous product and simplicial neural networks.

### Generative models

I am interested in connecting structured signal models with modern generative learning, including flow-based methods for spatiotemporal and graph-structured data.

### Biomedical and spatiotemporal applications

Applications include brain and EEG signals, seizure analysis, sleep staging, weather and traffic forecasting, and other biomedical signal and image problems.
